Share a budget of facilities among groups

Source: R/location.R
allocate_budget.Rd

Given, for each group (a municipality, a district), what its first, second, third... new facility would add, decides how many facilities each group gets out of a common budget, and in what order.

Usage

allocate_budget(
  curves,
  budget,
  groups = NULL,
  criterion = "utilitarian",
  weights = NULL,
  tiers = NULL,
  eligible = NULL
)

Arguments

curves

A data.frame with one row per facility of each group: group and marginal (what that facility adds, not negative), the rows of a group in the order of its facilities (or ordered by the column order, when there is one).

budget

How many facilities to share out. Fewer are given when the groups have no more facilities that add anything.

groups

A data.frame with one row per group: group, total (its demand) and, optionally, covered (the demand covered before any new facility; 0 without the column). NULL when the shares are not wanted; required by "maximin". A group may have no row in curves.

criterion

"utilitarian" or "maximin".

weights

The name of a column of groups with the weight of each group, above zero. NULL (default): every group weighs 1.

tiers

The name of a column of groups with the priority tier of each group, a whole number from 0, the lowest served first. NULL (default): one tier.

eligible

The name of a logical column of groups: whether each group may receive facilities. NULL (default): all may.

Value

A list of two tables:

  • steps: one row per facility, in the order they are given: order, group, marginal, covered (the demand covered in all the groups after it, what was covered before included) and lowest_share (the lowest share covered among the groups after it; NA without groups). The first k rows are the answer for a budget of k.

  • groups: one row per group: group, units (how many facilities it gets), gained, covered, share (NA without groups) and priority (the order in which the groups get their first facility: 1 for the first group to receive one, NA for a group that gets none).

    Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package).

Details

The curves come from locate_facilities() with model = "max_cover" and swap = FALSE, one call per group asking for as many facilities as there are candidates: the marginal column of sites is then what each further facility adds, and it does not increase.

With criterion = "utilitarian" each facility goes to the group where the next one adds most. Because the gains of a group do not increase, this covers the most demand possible, for the budget asked and for every smaller one (marginal analysis; Fox, 1966). With "maximin" each facility goes to the group with the lowest share of its demand covered that still has a facility to open, which gives the highest possible lowest share, again for every budget. Ties go to the larger gain, then to the group listed first. The difference between the covered of the two criteria for the same budget is what the fairer allocation costs (Bertsimas, Farias and Trichakis, 2011).

Weights, priority tiers and groups left out

Three columns of groups, named in weights, tiers and eligible, change who comes first.

  • weights: how much the demand of each group counts (say 2 where the need is most urgent, 1 elsewhere). "utilitarian" multiplies the gains of a group by its weight; as the weighted gains still do not increase, this is the largest weighted sum for every budget. "maximin" divides the share covered of a group by its weight, so that a group of weight 2 at 60% is served before one of weight 1 at 40%.

  • tiers: whole numbers, the lowest first. A facility only goes to a group when no group of a lower tier has one left to open that adds anything; within the tier the criterion decides. With "maximin" this is "the worst covered among the most urgent first".

  • eligible: FALSE for the groups that get no facility. They stay in the result with zero units and count in covered and in lowest_share.

The result is never weighted: marginal, covered, gained and the shares are demand as given, so that runs with and without the columns can be compared.

References

Bertsimas D, Farias VF, Trichakis N (2011). "The price of fairness." Operations Research, 59(1), 17-31. doi:10.1287/opre.1100.0865 .

Fox B (1966). "Discrete optimization via marginal analysis." Management Science, 13(3), 210-216. doi:10.1287/mnsc.13.3.210 .

See also

Other facility location: distance_matrix()

Examples

curves <- data.frame(
  group = c("north", "north", "north", "south", "south"),
  marginal = c(500, 200, 50, 400, 300)
)
groups <- data.frame(group = c("north", "south"), covered = c(1000, 0),
                     total = c(2000, 1000))
allocate_budget(curves, budget = 3, groups = groups)$steps
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   order group marginal covered lowest_share
#>   <int> <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1     1 north      500    1500          0  
#> 2     2 south      400    1900          0.4
#> 3     3 south      300    2200          0.7
allocate_budget(curves, budget = 3, groups = groups, criterion = "maximin")$steps
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   order group marginal covered lowest_share
#>   <int> <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1     1 south      400    1400          0.4
#> 2     2 south      300    1700          0.5
#> 3     3 north      500    2200          0.7

# the south counts double; then the north first, whatever it adds
groups$weight <- c(1, 2)
groups$tier <- c(0, 1)
allocate_budget(curves, budget = 3, groups = groups, weights = "weight")$groups
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   group units gained covered share priority
#>   <chr> <int>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 north     1    500    1500  0.75        2
#> 2 south     2    700     700  0.7         1
allocate_budget(curves, budget = 3, groups = groups, tiers = "tier")$groups
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   group units gained covered share priority
#>   <chr> <int>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 north     3    750    1750 0.875        1
#> 2 south     0      0       0 0           NA
